title: Take the rotten vegetables out of a packed produce container and put them in the waste bin
instruction: Take the rotten vegetables out of the produce container and put them in the waste bin.
context: Spoiled produce left among fresh produce is a food-safety hazard: USDA's Food Safety and Inspection Service notes that some molds produce mycotoxins that can make people sick (fsis.usda.gov, "Molds on Food"), so a spoiled piece has to be found and removed. The instruction does not say which pieces are spoiled: the robot has to see it, and the difficulty is physical as well: each tomato is 8.6-8.8 cm across and the gripper opens 9.4 cm, and the tomatoes stand 1 cm from the peppers beside them.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases (x forward, y to the robot's left); heights above the table top. Produce container: a Rubbermaid FreshWorks 3-gallon produce saver, clear plastic, 45.7 x 30.5 cm and 16.0 cm tall (18 x 12 x 6 5/16 in), lid and insert removed, walls about 3 mm, centred at (36.0, -3.0) with its long side along y, taped to the table. Waste bin: an OXO Good Grips Easy-Clean 1.75 gallon compost bin, charcoal plastic, 25.8 cm along x by 21.1 cm along y and 30.5 cm tall (10.15 x 8.3 x 12 in), lid open, centred at (40.0, -49.0), taped to the table. In the container, on its floor, centres at: rotten tomato A (29.5, -20.1); red bell pepper A (29.5, -9.6); rotten tomato B (29.5, 0.9); red bell pepper B (29.5, 11.4); zucchini (42.5, -14.7), its length along y. Each rotten tomato: a large red tomato (fresh produce), 8.8 x 8.6 x 5.9 cm, 220 g, stem end up, with a dark spoiled patch about 4 cm across on its upper shoulder beside the stem, firm enough to hold its shape and not leaking, turned so the patch faces the front of the table (towards the robots); about 1 cm clear of its neighbours along the row. Each red bell pepper (fresh produce): 8.5 x 10.2 x 10.2 cm, 170 g, stem up. Zucchini (fresh produce): 19.7 x 5.4 x 5.2 cm, 297 g, dark green. The rotten vegetables are the two tomatoes with the dark patch; the peppers and the zucchini are fresh. The left arm has nothing to do.
scoring: Tools: a phone camera, a ruler and the trial video. Before each trial, tape marks outline each good piece's starting place on the container floor. Fresh produce kept: both peppers and the zucchini lie inside the produce container's walls, each with its centre within 2 cm of its starting centre (ruler against the marks). In the bin: a tomato rests inside the bin's walls, below its rim. Released: both grippers are open and at least 7 cm from both tomatoes, and both tomatoes are still, held for 1 s in the video. At the end: 0 if any pepper or the zucchini is outside the container or more than 2 cm from its start, or no tomato is in the bin; 0.5 with one tomato in the bin; 0.75 with both in the bin but a gripper still within 7 cm of a tomato or a tomato still moving; 1.0 with both in the bin and released, held for 1 s.
reset_notes: Rotten tomatoes: buy firm large tomatoes about 8.5-9 cm across and 5.5-6.5 cm tall (200-240 g) and keep them at room temperature until a dark, sunken patch about 4 cm across has formed beside the stem; discard any that has split or leaks, and keep spares. Each trial use two such tomatoes, stem end up with the patch towards the robots, at the listed centres; stand the peppers and lay the zucchini back at theirs, checking the 1 cm gaps beside each tomato with a ruler and re-taping the outline marks. Cover each gripper pad with a fresh disposable nitrile glove fingertip for the trial, empty the bin, and wipe the table, containers and pads afterwards.
fidelity: Rigid-body PhysX at 240 Hz. Each piece of produce is one rigid body with a convex-hull collider, with the size and mass of its 3D asset (marso SimReady, CC BY 4.0): tomatoes do not squash or leak and the rot is a texture. The containers are fixed straight-walled boxes with 3 mm walls and floors (the real bin tapers; its lid is open and the produce container's lid and vented insert are removed).
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (1,200 steps; the right arm went to the zucchini and pushed it about at the back of the container for the whole run, and never touched a tomato or the bin); demo: 1.0
